पत्रं करंजशम्याकवंशार्कानामुपाहरेत्।। 
एतेषां स्वरसो ग्राह्यः नालिकेरोदकं तथा। 
पाचयेत्तैलमेरण्डं केरक्षीरेण संयुतम्।। 
कल्कार्थं रोहिणी व्योषं हिंगु मायाफलं तथा। 
षट्तण्डुलं च पारंगी केरातश्च रसोनकः।। 
पाकं कृत्वा विधिवत् भक्षयेत् आदरेण हि। 
विबन्धं नाशयेत् शीघ्रं श्वासं कासं च नाशयेत्।। (Sahasrayogam) 

 The verse describes preparation of castor oil processed with herbal juices, coconut derivatives, and pungent herbs, and explains its action in relieving obstruction, respiratory difficulty, cough, pain, swelling, and fever.
sections.composition:
I. Drava Dravyas (Liquid Ingredients) 

 Sphotya Bhujanga / Gaja Pippali (Scindapsus officinalis – Gajapippali) Fresh Juice – 40 ml 
 Bhringaraja (Eclipta alba – False Daisy) Fresh Juice – 40 ml 
 Putika (Holoptelea integrifolia – Indian Elm) Fresh Juice – 40 ml 
 Punarnava (Boerhavia diffusa – Spreading Hogweed) Fresh Juice – 40 ml 
 Karanja Patra (Pongamia pinnata – Indian Beech Leaf) Fresh Juice – 40 ml 
 Aragvadha Patra (Cassia fistula – Golden Shower Leaf) Fresh Juice – 40 ml 
 Vamsha Patra (Bambusa arundinacea – Bamboo Leaf) Fresh Juice – 40 ml 
 Arka Patra (Calotropis gigantea – Crown Flower Leaf) Fresh Juice – 40 ml 
 Neyavalli (Ipomoea sepiaria – Creeping Morning Glory) Fresh Juice – 40 ml 
 Lavana Valli (Paederia foetida – Skunk Vine) Fresh Juice – 40 ml 
 Ardraka (Zingiber officinale – Fresh Ginger) Juice – 40 ml 
 Narikela Jala (Cocos nucifera – Coconut Water) – 640 ml 
 Narikela Kshira (Cocos nucifera – Coconut Milk) – 640 ml 

 II. Taila Dravya 

 Eranda Taila (Ricinus communis – Castor Oil) – 640 ml 

 III. Kalka Dravyas (Paste Ingredients) 

 Katuki (Picrorhiza kurroa – Kutki) – 10 g 
 Sunthi (Zingiber officinale – Dry Ginger) – 10 g 
 Pippali (Piper longum – Long Pepper) – 10 g 
 Marica (Piper nigrum – Black Pepper) – 10 g 
 Hingu (Ferula asafoetida – Asafoetida Resin) – 10 g 
 Mayaphala (Quercus infectoria – Oak Gall) – 10 g 
 Dhanyaka (Coriandrum sativum – Coriander Seed) – 10 g 
 Ela (Elettaria cardamomum – Cardamom) – 10 g 
 Indrayava (Holarrhena antidysenterica – Kurchi Seed) – 10 g 
 Jyotishmati (Celastrus paniculatus – Intellect Tree Seed) – 10 g 
 Bakuci (Psoralea corylifolia – Babchi Seed) – 10 g 
 Vidanga (Embelia ribes – False Black Pepper) – 10 g 
 Bharangi (Clerodendrum serratum – Blue Glory) – 10 g 
 Kiratatikta (Swertia chirata – Chirata) – 10 g 
 Lashuna (Allium sativum – Garlic) – 10 g 
 Chinosana (Cinnamomum cassia – Chinese Cinnamon) – 10 g 
 Yavani (Trachyspermum ammi – Ajwain) – 10 g 
 Ajamoda (Apium graveolens – Wild Celery) – 10 g 

 Method Of Preparation 
 All liquid ingredients are combined in a suitable vessel. The kalka dravyas are powdered separately and triturated to form a smooth paste. Castor oil is added to the liquid mixture followed by incorporation of the prepared herbal paste. The entire combination is heated on mild fire following classical Sneha Paka procedure. Continuous stirring is maintained to ensure uniform processing and to prevent adhesion of the paste to the vessel. Heating is continued until the aqueous component evaporates completely and the oil remains in its original quantity. Proper completion is indicated by absence of moisture, characteristic aroma, and formation of a soft non-sticky residue of kalka. The oil is filtered while warm and stored in airtight glass containers. 
 Method Of Use 

 Internal administration in prescribed dose under medical supervision. 
 External application in the form of Abhyanga (therapeutic oil massage).

 Systemic detoxifying and channel-clearing effect 

 Clinical Indications 

 Vibandha (Constipation and obstruction) 
 Shwasa (Dyspnea / respiratory difficulty) 
 Kasa (Cough) 
 Shula (Pain conditions) 
 Shopha (Inflammatory swelling) 
 Sarva Jvara (Fever of various origins)
sections.precautions:
Use under supervision of a qualified Ayurvedic practitioner. Dosage and method of administration should be individualized. Store in airtight containers away from heat and moisture. 
 Conclusion 
 Shwasari Taila is a classical medicated oil prepared by processing castor oil with multiple herbal juices, coconut derivatives, and pungent bio-enhancing herbs through the traditional Sneha Paka method. The formulation is primarily indicated in respiratory disorders, digestive obstruction, inflammatory conditions, and fever. When prepared according to classical procedure and administered appropriately, it functions as a penetrating therapeutic oil that supports respiratory function, alleviates obstruction, and promotes systemic balance.

 Introduction
